full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J.: Respondent No: 1 as petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1990 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act for pre-emption: of the case land which was allowed by judgment and order dated 9-3-92. The purchaser-petitioners filed F. M. A. No. 52 of 1992 against the said judgment and order which was dismissed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 23-2-98 from which the purchaser-petitioners have preferred this petition for leave to appeal. 

 2. The case of respondent No. 1 was that his father was the owner of the case land and the building thereon. Respondent No. 1 was born on 16.5.69 and his father died during his minority on 9-9-74. He inherited .0310 acre of land and the share of the building from his father and became a co-sharer by inheritance. He came to know for the first time on 10-5-90 from Salamatullah Khan and Habibur Rahman that his share to the extent of .0310 acre of land and the share of the building have been transferred by false personation by two forged kabalas collusively and without consideration by two alleged sale deeds dated 24-3-78 and 19-9-78 for which his sister representing him instituted Title Suit No. 117 of 1986 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chandpur for a declaration that the alleged deeds are illegal, forged, collusive, without consideration and void. He also came to know for the first time on 10-5-90 from the said two persons that the purchaser-petitioners purchased .0200 acre of land and 3 annas share of the building thereon from his brother and one of his two mothers by a registered kabala dated 22-3-79 at a consideration of Tk. 30,000/-. He also came to know that the petitioners further purchased .008 acre of land and 1 anna share of the building there-on from Rokeya Begum, the predecessor of opposite party Nos. 12-20 in the pre-emption application by registered kabala dated 17-8-79 at a consideration of Tk. 15,000/-Petitioner No. 1 purchased .0270 acre of land and 4 annas 10 gondas share of the building thereon from opposite party Nos. 9 and 10 in the pre-emption application and from the said Rokeya Begum by another registered kabala dated 7-4-79 at a consideration of Tk. 34,000/- Petitioner No. 3 purchased .0123 acre of land and 2 annas share of the building thereon from opposite party No. 11 of the pre-emption application by a registered kabala dated 11-4-79 at a consideration of Tk. 18,000/-. Petitioner No. 2 pur-chased .2070 acre of land and 4 annas 10 gondas share of the building thereon from opposite party Nos. 4, 5 and 6 of the pre-emption application by another registered kabala dated 14-4-79 at a consideration of Tk. 34, 000/- and in this way the purchaser-petitioners purchased .0953 acre of land and 15 annas share of the building thereof at a total consideration of Tk. 1,31,000/-, but for these purchases no notice under section 23 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act was served upon respondent No. 1. Those kabalas were executed and registered when he was minor and he was ignorant about these transfers. 

 3. Respondent No. 1 attained majority on 16-5-87 and having come to know of these purchases for the first time on 10-5-90 he obtained certified copies of the deeds in question and deposited the statutory amount of Tk. 1,31,000/- along with 5% compensation and filed the case on 15-5-90 for pre-emption in respect of the said kabalas of the year 1979 under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act. 

 7. The High Court Division negative the first contention by holding that there is no clear decision from any higher Courts on section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act on this point but there are two decisions of the High Court Division namely, those contained in Hajee Majar Ullah Sowdagar Vs. Mvi. Nurul Haque & Ors., 23DLR 68 and Sree Jitendra Nath Howlader Vs. Sree Bisweswar Howlader and ors., 42 DLR 253 which are on analogous provisions of sec-tion 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and in which one single application for separate purchases by different sellers and purchasers have been held to be maintainable. 

 10. We find that respondent No. 1 as P.W. 1 stated in his examination-in-chief about Title Suit No. 117 of 1986 and made a categorical assertion that he did not know about that case before. There was no cross-examination on this assertion. We therefore cannot draw any conclusion from nowhere that respondent No, 1 was aware about the existence of the 1979 impugned kabalas in 1988.
